01 /

The person behind the pipelines

Hi, I’m Harsha.
I make data useful.

I’m a data engineer at ASM Technologies, working on the Applied Materials – GIS project. I develop data-processing workflows, improve Spark workloads, and help turn raw records into reliable datasets.

My foundation in electronics and communication engineering, followed by full-stack development, gave me a broad engineering perspective. Today, my focus is cloud data engineering: how data arrives, how it changes, and how people can use it with confidence.

Reliable data

Check quality before downstream use.

Repeatable work

Build transformations that can run again.

Thoughtful performance

Understand the workload before tuning it.

01 / KNOWLEDGE IN PRACTICE

Spark & Databricks

Process large datasets across a cluster, then turn the results into usable tables.

Apache Spark

A distributed processing engine that divides data work across multiple machines.

How I use it

I use Spark DataFrames and Spark SQL to process structured and semi-structured datasets.

  • Transform and combine large datasets.
  • Apply partitioning, caching, and join strategies to suit the workload.
Large-scale processing with a consistent transformation approach.

PySpark

The Python interface to Apache Spark, used to express distributed data transformations.

How I use it

I develop reusable transformations for ingestion, cleansing, business rules, and validation.

  • Process nested JSON and file-based datasets.
  • Use window functions and timestamps to retain the latest record.
Reusable processing logic that is easier to understand and maintain.

Databricks

A cloud platform for working with data, Spark compute, notebooks, SQL, and scheduled workloads.

How I use it

I work with Azure Databricks and AWS Databricks; my professional work includes Hadoop-to-Azure-Databricks migration support.

  • Develop PySpark and SQL processing workflows.
  • Use jobs and parameterized workflows for repeatable execution.
A shared environment for developing and running data workloads.

Delta Lake

A table storage layer that adds transactional reliability and table-management capabilities to data lakes.

How I use it

Delta Lake is part of my data-engineering toolkit for cloud-based data solutions.

  • Work with Delta-based tables in the Databricks ecosystem.
  • Connect raw-data processing with curated table outputs.
More dependable tables for downstream data consumption.

Python & SQL

Express business rules clearly, query data precisely, and automate repeatable work.

Python

A general-purpose programming language used for data processing and automation.

How I use it

I use Python to automate repetitive tasks and develop reusable processing logic.

  • Organize logic into reusable functions.
  • Work with APIs, data validation, and workflow automation.
Less repetitive effort and more consistent execution.

SQL & Spark SQL

Languages for querying, joining, aggregating, and transforming tabular data.

How I use it

I write transformations and analytical queries, and tune queries for data-processing workloads.

  • Use joins, aggregations, and window functions.
  • Build SQL dashboards from Databricks System Tables.
Clear business logic and easier analysis of datasets and workloads.

Shell scripting

A way to automate commands and routine tasks in Linux and UNIX environments.

How I use it

I combine shell scripting with Python for repetitive operational and support tasks.

  • Run repeatable command-line workflows.
  • Work in Linux, UNIX, and RHEL environments.
Repeatable execution of routine engineering tasks.

REST APIs & Postman

APIs let applications exchange information; Postman helps inspect and test HTTP requests.

How I use it

My toolkit includes Databricks REST APIs, Postman, and API-based automation.

  • Work with request parameters and responses.
  • Use programmatic workflows for reporting and automation.
A practical bridge between data platforms and other tools.
03 / KNOWLEDGE IN PRACTICE

Pipeline development

Define how data is ingested, transformed, checked, and delivered, with a clear purpose at each step.

ETL & ELT

ETL transforms data before loading it to a target; ELT loads it first and transforms it there.

How I use it

I design and develop pipelines using PySpark, SQL, and Databricks Workflows.

  • Separate ingestion, cleansing, business rules, and output generation.
  • Use reusable and parameterized transformations.
A repeatable path from source data to business-ready datasets.

Incremental processing

Process new or changed records instead of repeatedly processing an entire dataset.

How I use it

I use timestamps, watermarks, and business keys to identify records that need processing.

  • Track a processing boundary with timestamps or watermarks.
  • Use business keys when identifying new and changed records.
More focused processing as source datasets grow.

Deduplication & reconciliation

Deduplication resolves repeated records; reconciliation checks that source and target data agree.

How I use it

I implement window-function logic and validate record counts and business keys.

  • Retain the latest record using timestamps.
  • Check duplicates, nulls, schema consistency, and record counts.
Cleaner outputs and greater confidence in pipeline results.

Data formats & modeling

Formats define how data is stored; models organize data for its intended use.

How I use it

I process CSV, JSON, Parquet, and ORC, including nested and semi-structured records.

  • Transform incoming structures for downstream consumption.
  • Apply consistent fields and business rules to outputs.
Data that downstream users and systems can work with.
04 / KNOWLEDGE IN PRACTICE

Cloud & storage

Work with cloud platforms, data-lake storage, and relational databases as parts of a complete data solution.

Azure & AWS

Cloud platforms that provide managed infrastructure and data services.

How I use it

My cloud experience includes Azure Databricks, AWS Databricks, ADLS Gen2, and AWS MSK.

  • Use cloud services within data-processing solutions.
  • Connect data ingestion, storage, and compute workflows.
Flexible building blocks for cloud-based data engineering.

ADLS Gen2

Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 provides cloud storage suited to analytical data lakes.

How I use it

I use ADLS Gen2 as the cloud data-lake layer for ingestion, transformation, and curated processing.

  • Read and process source datasets from the lake.
  • Organize storage around ingestion and downstream processing needs.
A shared storage foundation for data-engineering workloads.

MySQL & Azure SQL

Relational databases that organize data into tables queried with SQL.

How I use it

My database toolkit includes MySQL and Azure SQL.

  • Use SQL to query and work with relational data.
  • Understand tables, joins, keys, and structured data relationships.
Structured storage and predictable querying for relational datasets.

Hadoop migration

Moving workloads from a legacy Hadoop environment to a cloud data platform.

How I use it

I supported enterprise-scale migration of legacy Hadoop workloads to Azure Databricks.

  • Work with distributed processing concepts across platforms.
  • Support cloud-based processing of existing workloads.
A path from legacy processing to a cloud data environment.
05 / KNOWLEDGE IN PRACTICE

Quality & performance

Check correctness, understand how workloads execute, and tune the parts that matter.

Data-quality checks

Rules that identify missing, repeated, inconsistent, or invalid data.

How I use it

I develop checks for nulls, duplicates, schema consistency, record counts, and business keys.

  • Validate transformations before output consumption.
  • Use reconciliation to compare source and processed records.
More trustworthy datasets for downstream users.

Spark optimization

Adjust how Spark reads, combines, and processes data to fit the workload.

How I use it

I use partitioning, caching, broadcast joins, and shuffle optimization.

  • Inspect execution plans before choosing an optimization.
  • Choose caching or join strategies when appropriate to data size and reuse.
Avoid unnecessary processing and improve workload efficiency.

Monitoring & cost analysis

Observe workload behavior and resource usage to identify issues and improvement opportunities.

How I use it

I build SQL dashboards using Databricks System Tables.

  • Analyze DBU consumption and workload performance.
  • Look at utilization and cost patterns across processing workloads.
Better visibility into how the data platform is being used.

Job monitoring & error handling

Track execution outcomes and investigate failures in data-processing workflows.

How I use it

My experience includes job monitoring, production troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis.

  • Investigate failed processing tasks.
  • Work with other engineering teams to resolve production issues.
More dependable day-to-day pipeline execution.
06 / KNOWLEDGE IN PRACTICE

Streaming & delivery

Move events into processing workflows and make data work easier to run and share.

Apache Kafka & AWS MSK

Kafka carries event streams; MSK is AWS’s managed service for Kafka.

How I use it

I work with Kafka and AWS MSK for streaming-data ingestion and downstream workflow integration.

  • Connect streaming ingestion with processing workflows.
  • Work with event-driven data alongside batch workloads.
A way to bring continuously arriving data into the platform.

Databricks Workflows

Scheduled and coordinated tasks for running data-processing jobs.

How I use it

I use parameterized jobs and Databricks Workflows in ETL/ELT development.

  • Make processing repeatable across runs.
  • Coordinate the execution of pipeline tasks.
Consistent delivery of recurring data-processing work.

Catalog, sharing & SQL tools

Unity Catalog organizes and governs data; Delta Sharing shares it; SQL Warehouses support SQL workloads.

How I use it

My Databricks toolkit includes Unity Catalog, Delta Sharing, SQL Warehouses, and Genie.

  • Work within the platform’s data organization and access model.
  • Use SQL tools for querying and analysis.
Data that can be discovered, accessed, and consumed appropriately.

Git & engineering tools

Version control and development tools support a repeatable engineering workflow.

How I use it

I use Git, VS Code, Postman, Jira, and ServiceNow, with a background in full-stack development.

  • Track code changes and collaborate around engineering work.
  • Use development and issue-tracking tools across the workflow.
A clearer path from a code change to a maintained solution.
